Governance data, not build output.

THREE DISPOSITIONS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM SUPPRESSES.

`waived` with a valid `attestation` — a human signed that this specific sentence needs no test. Suppresses the untagged count. The reason must be unique: if the same reason fits two claims it is naming neither.

`waived` without an attestation — a PROPOSAL. Drafted by whoever wrote the code. Does NOT suppress. It is a request for a human to read one sentence.

`acknowledged` — measured technical debt. Nobody has read it. Does NOT suppress, and counts toward the ceiling, because unjudged prose IS unreviewed governance material. It used to suppress, which made bulk-acknowledging into bulk-waiving with a nicer word — 41 claims went through that door on 2026-08-20.

THE CEILING IS A CAPABILITY BOUNDARY, NOT A SETTING. Lowering it is ordinary. Raising it increases the unjudged surface the system tolerates, which is an authority-expanding operation, and needs a signed `ceiling_raise` from a registered human. The reason does not matter; the direction does. Verified 2026-08-23: before this rule, editing 1309 to 99999 was accepted in silence.

THE CURRENT 1407 IS THE HONEST NUMBER. The previous 1309 excluded 97 acknowledged items and 1 unsigned waiver that were suppressing without anyone having read them. Nothing was added to the repo; the measurement was corrected. It still requires a human signature, because 'the measurement changed' is exactly the reasoning this gate exists to refuse on its own.
